To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the success of a forum depends upon its size and the ease of monitoring its members; 2) the size of a forum is limited by the cost of monitoring its members and the ease of finding a forum that provides a similar service; 3) forums that have a high rate of new members and low connectivity are less successful than those that have low rates of new members and high connectivity.

the success of underground forums is contingent on: (1) easy and inexpensive monitoring of the forum community, (2) moderate increase in new forum members, (3) small world effect in forum connectivity, (4) limited privileged access, and (5) enforcement of bans and/or fines on offending members.
the success of underground forums is contingent upon the ability of the community to enforce norms of cooperation and the ability to monitor the actions of the community.
